MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
Cloud Infrastructure & DevOps | CI/CD and Test Infrastructure
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with hands-on experience building CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral environments and test infrastructure for three product teams. Uses GitLab CI, Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes access at work; also builds and operates a personal k3s homelab using GitOps, monitoring and Terraform-provisioned Hetzner infrastructure. Experienced in improving pipeline performance and reliability, documenting technical processes, and working across QA, product and development teams. Transitioning toward cloud infrastructure and platform engineering.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Terraform (personal projects), Argo CD, GitOps
Containers & Platforms: Kubernetes (namespace-level access at work), k3s, Linux
Monitoring & Data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL
Programming & Automation: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, Ansible (basic)
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by profiling pipelines, parallelising test jobs, adding dependency caching and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%.
- Built short-lived merge-request environments for application services, PostgreSQL and seeded data, deployed through GitLab CI using Docker Compose and later Helm on the shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Built a Python and PostgreSQL pipeline-results workflow and Grafana dashboards to help teams identify flaky tests and prioritise fixes.
- Write Bash and Python tools for PostgreSQL test-data seeding.
- Wrote the internal guide to CI workflows used in team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects through manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS

Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices and deployed applications from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Implemented short-lived environments for application services, PostgreSQL and seeded data, deployed via Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI.
- Enabled QA and product teams to review changes before merge and run end-to-end tests against each environment; automated cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelised test jobs, introduced dependency caching and separated end-to-end tests into their own stage.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation in progress; exam scheduled for January 2027

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, professional, and unusually credible for a QA-to-DevOps transition. It uses quantified outcomes effectively: pipeline duration decreased from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs decreased by about 30%, and flaky tests decreased from 7% to below 1%. The separation of professional experience and selected infrastructure projects makes the candidate's infrastructure direction clear without overstating production ownership. Scope is also described accurately, especially the distinction between namespace-level Kubernetes access at work and the personal k3s/Hetzner environment. The main content limitation is that the strongest evidence is concentrated in CI and test infrastructure rather than broader cloud infrastructure, networking, security, and systems design.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly: standard section headings, simple text structure, conventional dates, clear job titles, and searchable technology keywords such as Terraform, Kubernetes, GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, Linux, AWS EC2, S3, Prometheus, Grafana, and Argo CD. It should parse reliably and has a reasonably strong AI-screening probability for junior or transitional DevOps/platform roles. For this specific contractor role, screening probability is lower because the CV does not contain Terragrunt, mTLS, networking, systems architecture/design, or substantial AWS operations evidence. The keyword coverage is appropriately truthful; unsupported terms should not be added merely to mirror the advertisement.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the role's infrastructure-engineering, CI/CD, observability, analytical-thinking, communication, and stakeholder-collaboration aspects. The strongest matches are ownership of pipelines for three teams, ephemeral environment design, Helm/Kubernetes deployment, monitoring, Terraform use in a personal cloud environment, measurable reliability improvements, technical documentation, and collaboration with QA and product teams. AWS is shown only at a basic personal-learning level, which is a partial match rather than production AWS experience. The candidate's material does not establish strong Terraform or any Terragrunt experience, broad cloud environment operation, systems architecture/design, mTLS, network design, practical security ownership, IoT/remote-device integration, backend development, or virtual-machine administration. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than CV-writing defects. The CV is a strong truthful match for an entry-level or developing platform/DevOps profile, but a weaker match for the advertised contractor who is expected to shape production fleet-connectivity architecture independently.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENT:
1. In the Technical Skills section, add "Git" to an appropriate category, such as "Infrastructure & CI/CD: Git, GitLab CI, Jenkins...", because the candidate's project material explicitly states that applications are deployed from a Git repository and Git is present in the original skills.
2. In the Professional Summary, make the target level and strongest transferable match more explicit without overstating seniority. For example, change the final sentence to: "Transitioning into cloud infrastructure and platform engineering, bringing hands-on experience with infrastructure-as-code, Kubernetes-based test environments, CI/CD ownership, observability, and cross-team technical enablement." This is supported by the documented Terraform, Kubernetes, monitoring, pipeline ownership, documentation, and mentoring experience.
3. In the Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps project, make the Terraform scope slightly more precise for recruiter and ATS interpretation by changing "Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform" to "Provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and deployed/operated Kubernetes workloads on a personal k3s homelab." Keep the personal-project context visible; do not imply production cloud ownership.
4. In the Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments project, retain the existing scope clarification and add the stakeholder outcome already supported by the source material: "Enabled QA and product teams to review changes before merge and run end-to-end tests against each environment." This is already present in substance, but it should remain prominent because it demonstrates stakeholder enablement and systems delivery rather than only tool usage.
5. In Certifications & Professional Development, retain the explicit wording "CKA preparation in progress; exam scheduled for January 2027" and do not shorten it to "CKA" or "Certified Kubernetes Administrator." The current wording is truthful and prevents ATS or recruiter misinterpretation that the certification has already been obtained.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible transition CV with clear progression from QA automation into CI/CD and infrastructure work. It uses quantified outcomes effectively, including reducing pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, lowering runner costs by about 30%, and reducing flaky tests below 1%. The summary is appropriately transparent about namespace-level Kubernetes access, personal infrastructure work, and the transition toward platform engineering. The main content weakness is duplication: the Professional Experience section and Selected Infrastructure Projects repeat the same Odrava initiatives. This makes the CV longer without adding much new evidence. The document also does not clearly distinguish production/team infrastructure experience from personal homelab experience in every relevant section, although the current wording is generally truthful and does not appear to hallucinate experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly overall: it uses conventional headings, plain text section structure, readable date formats, standard job titles, and relevant keywords such as GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Docker, Linux, Prometheus, Grafana, PostgreSQL, Python, Bash, and AWS. It should parse reliably. AI screening probability for this particular role is moderate rather than high because the CV does not contain supported evidence for several high-priority terms in the advertisement, especially Terragrunt, mTLS, network design, systems architecture/system design, and cloud infrastructure operation at production scale. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than formatting defects and should not be filled with unsupported claims. The use of both Professional Experience and Selected Infrastructure Projects is acceptable, but the duplicated project content may dilute keyword relevance and recruiter attention.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with hands-on CI/CD and test infrastructure, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes application deployment, observability, Linux, analytical improvement, and technical documentation. The candidate also shows relevant AWS exposure at a basic personal-learning level and JVM-adjacent experience through Java test automation. The CV is less aligned with the role's core cloud-infrastructure scope: strong Terraform and Terragrunt, AWS or another major-cloud production environment, systems architecture, networking, mutual TLS, security, train-to-cloud or remote-device integration, and leading infrastructure proposals from idea to production. The homelab demonstrates initiative and practical learning, but it should remain clearly labelled as personal infrastructure rather than being presented as employment experience. The evidence for stakeholder engagement is present but understated: the candidate wrote an onboarding guide, supported QA and product review workflows, and mentored two interns. The document should make those truthful leadership and communication examples more visible. No direct IoT, automotive, or remote-device integration experience is present.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, keep the strongest infrastructure achievements and remove or substantially shorten the duplicated descriptions in Selected Infrastructure Projects. For example, retain the detailed ephemeral-environment and pipeline-speed bullets under Odrava, then reduce each corresponding project entry to one concise line or remove the duplicate project entries entirely. This will improve focus and prevent the same evidence from being counted repeatedly.

2. In the Professional Summary, make the role-relevant scope more explicit without overstating seniority. Change the final sentence from "Transitioning toward cloud infrastructure and platform engineering" to wording such as: "Transitioning from QA automation into cloud infrastructure and platform engineering, with hands-on experience in CI/CD, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, infrastructure automation, observability and Linux-based systems." Keep the existing namespace-level qualification so the scope remains accurate.

3. In the Odrava Health Software experience, make the stakeholder and technical-leadership evidence more visible. Add or revise a bullet to state: "Authored the internal CI workflow guide used for team onboarding and coordinated with QA, product and development teams to make merge-request environments available for review and end-to-end testing." This is supported by the candidate information and aligns with leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along without claiming formal infrastructure leadership.

4. In the Personal Infrastructure Project section, clarify the boundary between personal and professional experience in the heading and bullets. Use a heading such as "Personal Infrastructure Project — Homelab k3s Cluster and Hetzner VPS" and retain wording such as "personal Hetzner VPS" and "personal project." Do not move it into an employer role or describe it as production infrastructure, because the candidate information identifies it as a homelab and personal account project.

5. In the Technical Skills section, make the strength and scope of Terraform more precise. Change "Terraform (personal projects)" to "Terraform (personal Hetzner infrastructure project)" and keep Ansible explicitly labelled "basic." Do not add Terragrunt, stronger Terraform proficiency, AWS production experience, mTLS, or network-design claims, because they are not supported by the candidate information.

6. In the Certifications & Professional Development section, retain the transparent status of the Kubernetes credential. Use wording such as "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam scheduled for January 2027 — not yet certified." This avoids any possibility that an ATS or recruiter interprets the entry as an achieved certification.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into DevOps and cloud infrastructure. The summary is targeted, the experience bullets are specific and quantified, and the pipeline, ephemeral-environment, monitoring, and homelab work is presented credibly. The document communicates ownership, analytical problem-solving, collaboration, and measurable outcomes well. The personal infrastructure project is correctly labelled as personal rather than being presented as employment experience, which protects credibility. Minor content omissions include the candidate’s total seven years of experience and Git/GitLab API, both of which are supported by the original candidate information and would improve completeness.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-friendly: it uses standard section headings, readable text formatting, conventional chronology, clear technology categories, and strong keyword coverage for GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, Argo CD, GitOps, Linux, Python, Bash, PostgreSQL, Prometheus, Grafana, and AWS. Quantified achievements should parse well and are also likely to perform well in AI screening. However, screening probability for this specific role will be limited by genuine requirement gaps rather than formatting: Terragrunt, mTLS, networking, system design, and broader cloud infrastructure operation are not demonstrated. Terraform is explicitly limited to a personal Hetzner project, and AWS is correctly described as basic learning. Do not add unsupported keywords merely to improve ATS matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the practical CI/CD, test infrastructure, ephemeral Kubernetes environment, observability, Linux, analytical, documentation, and cross-team collaboration aspects of the role. It shows ownership through the GitLab CI pipelines, technical enablement through the internal workflow guide, and stakeholder engagement with QA, product, and development teams. AWS is present at a basic learning level, and Java provides a limited JVM-related connection through test automation. The candidate’s material shows gaps against several core requirements: strong Terraform and Terragrunt; systems architecture and system design; networking including mTLS; broader practical security awareness; IoT, automotive, or remote-device integration; and virtual-machine experience. The document should not imply production Kubernetes ownership, because the candidate has namespace-level access and the platform team operates the cluster. The strongest truthful positioning is an early-career infrastructure/platform engineer with substantial CI/CD and environment automation experience, rather than a fully experienced cloud infrastructure architect.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary section, add the supported duration of experience to improve seniority clarity. For example, change the opening to: "QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused primarily on CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral environments and build/test infrastructure." Keep the existing transition-to-platform-engineering sentence after it.
2. In the TECHNICAL SKILLS section, add "Git" under Infrastructure & CI/CD or a separate "Version Control & Delivery" category, because Git is listed in the original candidate information and is relevant to GitOps and infrastructure-as-code repositories.
3. In the TECHNICAL SKILLS section, add "GitLab API" under Programming & Automation or Monitoring & Data. The candidate’s original portfolio states that the flaky-test dashboard used the GitLab API, so this is a supported keyword relevant to automation and platform integration.
4. In the Personal Infrastructure Project section, change "cert-manager for TLS" to "cert-manager for TLS certificate management". This uses the job advertisement’s security terminology more precisely without claiming unsupported mutual TLS.
5. In the Professional Summary and skills wording, retain the current scope qualifiers—"namespace-level Kubernetes access at work," "personal Hetzner infrastructure project," and "AWS ... basics." Do not replace them with broader claims such as "managed Kubernetes clusters," "strong Terraform," "AWS infrastructure," or "cloud architecture," because those claims are not supported by the original candidate information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, professional, and supported by strong quantified achievements. The strongest evidence is the GitLab CI ownership, reduction of pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, 30% runner-cost reduction, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, observability dashboards, and documented onboarding processes. The document is also appropriately transparent about namespace-level Kubernetes access, personal Terraform use, basic Ansible, AWS learning, and the fact that the CKA is not yet obtained. The main content limitation is that the professional work and personal infrastructure project are presented in a way that could make the scope of production infrastructure ownership less immediately clear. The selected-projects section also repeats two achievements already described under Odrava Health.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is strong: standard section headings, conventional chronology, clear technology lists, quantified results, and relevant terms such as Terraform, Kubernetes, GitLab CI, Helm, Docker, Linux, Prometheus, Grafana, Argo CD, GitOps, AWS, and TLS certificate management are present. The document should parse reliably because it does not use tables, columns, graphics, or unusual formatting. AI screening probability is moderate to strong for adjacent junior/mid-level DevOps or platform roles, but lower for this specific position because the CV does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mTLS, network design, production cloud operations, or system-design ownership. Those are candidate-experience gaps rather than ATS wording defects and should not be claimed or added without evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV shows relevant hands-on infrastructure engineering through CI/CD infrastructure, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, Helm deployments, monitoring, GitOps, and a Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS. It also shows analytical thinking, clear technical documentation, ownership of technical workflows, and collaboration with QA and product stakeholders. AWS is present only as personal learning, which matches the candidate material but is weaker than professional AWS experience. The document does not show strong Terraform and Terragrunt, full systems architecture or system-design responsibility, mTLS, network design, practical security ownership, IoT or automotive integration, or backend/full-stack development. Java is limited to test code rather than JVM backend work. Linux is shown, but virtual-machine experience is not. The candidate's background is therefore a credible adjacent match for a junior-to-mid DevOps or platform-oriented role, but only a partial match for this contractor role's senior infrastructure, networking, security, and architecture expectations. The collaborative and ownership-oriented culture is reasonably supported by pipeline ownership, cross-team work, documentation, mentoring, and environments used by QA and product teams.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified; the document's additional technologies and project details are supported by the Original Candidate Information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the role target and strongest job-relevant evidence more direct. Replace the opening and closing sentences with wording such as: "QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including 2 years building and operating CI/CD and test infrastructure across three product teams. Hands-on with GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, namespace-level Kubernetes environments, observability, GitOps, and Terraform for personal Hetzner infrastructure; now targeting cloud infrastructure and platform engineering work." This keeps the transition truthful while placing the most relevant evidence earlier.
2. In the Technical Skills section, rename "Cloud learning" to "Cloud (personal learning)" and keep the qualification explicit: "AWS: EC2, S3 basics (personal learning)". This improves ATS matching for AWS without implying professional AWS experience.
3. In the Technical Skills section, add supported infrastructure keywords that are currently demonstrated elsewhere: "Infrastructure as Code," "Observability," "TLS certificate management," and "GitOps." For example: "Infrastructure & Delivery: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Terraform, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Argo CD, GitOps, Infrastructure as Code" and "Observability & Security: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, cert-manager, TLS certificate management." Do not add mTLS, network design, or security tools that are not supported by the candidate information.
4. In the Professional Experience section, retitle "Personal Infrastructure Project — Homelab k3s Cluster and Hetzner VPS" as "Personal Infrastructure Project — Homelab k3s Cluster and Terraform-Provisioned Hetzner VPS". This makes the infrastructure-as-code evidence easier for both ATS and recruiters to identify while clearly preserving its personal-project status.
5. Under the Odrava Health role, revise the ephemeral-environment bullet to include the stakeholder outcome already supported by the project material: "Built short-lived merge-request environments containing application services, PostgreSQL, and seeded data, deployed through GitLab CI using Docker Compose and later Helm on the shared Kubernetes cluster; enabled QA and product reviews and end-to-end testing, with automatic cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity." This more directly demonstrates stakeholder collaboration and support for deployable, testable services.
6. Remove or consolidate the duplicate "Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments" and "CI Pipeline Speed-up" entries in Selected Infrastructure Projects, or label the section "Selected Infrastructure Projects and Outcomes" and shorten each entry to one distinct line. The same achievements already appear under Odrava Health; reducing repetition would create space and make the CV feel more focused.
7. In the Certifications & Professional Development section, use a clearly separated format to prevent automated systems from misreading the planned exam as a completed certification: "ISTQB Foundation Level — Certified, 2019" and "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) — Preparation in progress; exam scheduled January 2027; not yet certified."
